_note: Pepin's own voice loop, the cascade (scripts/voice_cascade.py, pepin.voice_cascade): local ears (loudness gate + Whisper on the Mac) -> Claude as the talker (streamed, prompt-cached, the robot's tools) -> local voice (Qwen3-TTS on the Mac) -> the board's speaker. Every key can be switched for one run with --set section.key=value. Costs are ESTIMATES from the prices below and the API's own token counts.

ears.note: wake name: a conversation opens only on the robot's name (pepin.voice_live.wake.is_wake); always: every utterance is a turn (the bench). silence_s: the end of the turn is this much quiet after the last loud frame (0.4 s; 0.5 s was the Live gate's). 2026-10-09, 18 of Artem's live utterances with 0.25 s of quiet inserted mid-sentence (scratch/voice_cascade_eot/eot_eval.py): silence 0.5 closed 2-3 of them early, 0.4 3-4, Smart Turn 0.5 15-16, Smart Turn 0.85 13-15; with the continuation merge none stayed cut (the voice always came back within 0.8 s); the close after the last word: 500, 400, 220 (max 500), 220 (max 400 with silence 0.4) ms. start_db: a frame this far above the room's floor is loud. vad_open: a loud frame opens an utterance only when the barge-in's Silero model gives speech at least this probability (0: loudness alone); 2026-10-11 the room's rustles at -46..-32 dBFS opened 20-30 phantom utterances a minute over the -85 floor and each phantom in the 0.8 s after a phrase held the turn ~2 s. lead_s: the audio kept from before the opening; Silero says speech only ~0.4 s into a word (measured on 'как у тебя дела'), so with the old 0.3 s the first word was lost ('у тебя дела'). floor_min_dbfs: the floor never follows the room below this (-85: the XVF3800's noise suppression delivers -90..-94 dBFS between words, 2026-10-09 logs, so a higher floor would call quiet syllables silence; macOS say pads with digital silence; a floor that low opened the gate on -84 dBFS hiss for 15 s at a time, read by Whisper as 'Продолжение следует...'); speech sits at -50..-20 dBFS. continuation_s: the person starting again this soon after an utterance closed (by the model or the silence), before any of the reply was played, cancels the brain's call and the two utterances become one turn (2026-10-09: Smart Turn closed 'сегодня день.' at p 0.97 and the rest of the sentence came as the next turn); 0: off. Once the reply plays, it is a barge-in (flags.barge_in). turn_model: null (the fixed silence alone), smart-turn-v3.2 (the sound alone) or two-gates (the words of the early read and the sound together); the turn section

turn.two_gates_note: with ears.turn_model two-gates (pepin.voice_cascade.turn_text): the transcriber's early read of a pause (transcriber.early_s 0.15; GigaAM ~35 ms, so the words are judged ~0.2 s into the pause, on the transcriber's thread, no extra call) says complete, incomplete or unsure. Russian rules: incomplete when the last word is a conjunction, preposition, negation, hesitation or intensifier, on 'потому что'/'то есть', openers or the robot's name alone, a question word not read as a question, a trailing comma; complete for a read sentence of two words or more (GigaAM ends every prefix with '.' or '?', so the mark only says it was read). The words complete and the sound agreeing (acoustic pause: the pause itself; smart-turn-v3.2: its p >= threshold, asked at min_silence_s) close the utterance at early_close_s of quiet; words incomplete hold it open to incomplete_s; anything else closes it at ears.silence_s. A continuation (back within ears.continuation_s) is judged with the words before it. text_model namo-ru (videosdk-live Namo-Turn-Detector-v1-Russian, Apache-2.0, 136 MB int8 ONNX, ~13 ms on the CPU) is a second opinion: p <= incomplete_p vetoes (wait), p >= complete_p makes a lone word whole. 2026-10-12, scripts/turn_eval.py (203 of Artem's turns: 148 from the cascade records of 10-11/12, 55 Live cuts of 10-08; and 307 mid-sentence pauses made by inserting quiet at word boundaries), turns cut before the last word / the close after it p50 (mean) ms: as spoken, silence 0.4 8 / 400 (535), silence 0.25 12 / 260 (349), Smart Turn 0.5 13 / 220 (319), two-gates 12 / 260 (367), two-gates early_close_s 0.3 12 / 300 (414); pauses +0.25 s cut: silence 0.4 14, 0.25 37, Smart Turn 0.5 263, 0.85 225, two-gates 27, two-gates 0.3 20, with Smart Turn 0.85 as the sound 24; pauses +0.5 s: silence 0.4 285, 0.25 299, Smart Turn 300, two-gates 262, with namo-ru 243 (but 10 of 203 finished turns waited 0.8 s); pauses +0.8 s: all 295-304, the continuation merge joins ~95 %. The rules call 83 % of true ends complete and 1 % incomplete, 56 % of mid-sentence pause reads complete (a finished-looking prefix) and 11 % incomplete
turn.note: with ears.turn_model smart-turn-v3.2 (pipecat-ai/smart-turn-v3, smart-turn-v3.2-cpu.onnx: 8 MB int8 ONNX on the CPU, BSD-2-Clause, 23 languages with Russian at 93.5 % on its own benchmark; ~9 ms a call here): at min_silence_s of quiet inside an utterance the model reads its last window_s seconds (zeros in front, as it was trained) on a worker thread, and the utterance closes when it says p >= threshold (0.85: at 0.5 it cut 'сегодня день.' live at p 0.97, and at either it fires in most 0.25 s mid-sentence pauses, which the continuation merge joins back); otherwise ears.silence_s closes it as before. Every turn logs p, the model's own ms and the time saved against the fixed silence

gigaam.timings_note: each word's time from the 40 ms frames the decoder emitted its tokens at (onnx-asr with_timestamps, BPE tokens for the e2e models, letters for -ctc/-rnnt), its log-prob, and its vowels from the sound (Praat voicing within 10 dB of the word's loudest step, pepin.voice_cascade.timing): the prosody tag's stretch phrase reads them, the heard event logs them (words: w, t, lp, v). Same model call: 2026-10-12 (scratch/gigaam_timing_1012/timed_cost.py), +0-4 ms on 2-4 s utterances and +10 ms on 6.8 s over the plain read's 52-99 ms. false: the text alone
gigaam.note: GigaAM v3 (Sber, MIT), Russian only, on onnxruntime's CPU (pepin.voice_cascade.stt.gigaam). uv sync --group stt-gigaam. model: gigaam-v3-e2e-rnnt or -e2e-ctc (punctuation and capitals), gigaam-v3-rnnt or -ctc (lower case); quantization int8 halves the memory. 2026-10-12, 3 of Artem's cuts (2.6-4.1 s) on the M5 Pro beside the stack (tests/models): loads in 0.9 s, footprint +0.93 GB (int8 +0.5), 56 ms an utterance with 4 threads (Whisper turbo on the GPU 201 ms, +2.6 GB); closed, onnxruntime keeps ~0.4 GB of freed buffers that the next load reuses

parakeet.note: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 (CC-BY-4.0), 25 European languages, no language input, on the GPU through mlx-audio (pepin.voice_cascade.stt.parakeet). uv sync --group stt-parakeet. dtype: the stored float32 cast once loaded (null keeps float32, 2.5 GB). 2026-10-12, the same 3 cuts: loads in 5.6 s, footprint +1.55 GB, 29 ms an utterance

canary.note: NVIDIA Canary 1B v2 (CC-BY-4.0), 25 European languages, transcriber.language forced, on onnxruntime's CPU (pepin.voice_cascade.stt.canary). uv sync --group stt-canary. quantization null: the full model, ~4 GB. 2026-10-12, the same 3 cuts: loads in 1.6 s, footprint +2.2 GB, 199 ms an utterance with 4 threads

voxtral.note: Mistral Voxtral Mini 4B Realtime (Apache-2.0), 13 languages, no language input, on the GPU through mlx-audio (pepin.voice_cascade.stt.voxtral), 3.1 GB of 4-bit weights. uv sync --group stt-voxtral. delay_ms: the transcription delay (null: the model's 480 ms); a whole utterance costs one decoder step per 80 ms of it: 2026-10-12, the same 3 cuts, loads in 7.4 s, footprint +5.0 GB, 1.9 s an utterance (33 ms a step); for the record, not for talking

transcriber.note: Whisper large-v3-turbo, Russian forced. engine mlx: on the Mac's GPU (mlx-whisper); whispercpp: whisper.cpp's server with the encoder on the Neural Engine through CoreML and the decoder on the CPU (pepin.voice_live.whisper_cpp; whispercpp.dir holds bin/whisper-server and models/ggml-<model>.bin beside its -encoder.mlmodelc). 2026-10-09, 15 of Artem's cuts x3 on the M5 Pro (scratch/whisper_ane/bench.py), p50 ms quiet / 12 busy CPU cores / a GPU matmul loop: mlx turbo 174 / 185 / 565, whispercpp turbo 435 / 578 / 445, whispercpp large-v3 842 / 1789 / 976; the GPU runs the 32-layer encoder 2.5x faster than the Neural Engine, so mlx stays the default and whispercpp is the engine for a busy GPU (the voice, the depth and localisation nets), using 0.5 core and no GPU. Words against mlx: turbo 6 edits in 92 words, large-v3 3, the wake name found alike. One run: --set transcriber.engine=whispercpp (whispercpp.model large-v3 for the slower large model); while running: scripts/voice_cascade.py switch --transcriber whispercpp, which writes the key transcriber of data/voice/control.json ('mlx', 'whispercpp', 'whispercpp:large-v3' or {engine, model}; the file's one reader is pepin.voice_cascade.control.ControlFile, with brain and voice beside it) and prints the loop's answer, acted on when the file changes, the new engine loaded beside the old one and swapped between utterances. coreml_units: ane (CPU and Neural Engine), all (CoreML picks the GPU here: 236 ms), gpu, cpu (912 ms); gpu: the decoder on Metal. The first start of an encoder compiles it for the Neural Engine (34 s turbo, 27 s large-v3, once; then 1-3 s). early_s: Whisper starts on an utterance at this much quiet inside it, while the end-of-turn silence is still running, so its words are ready when the utterance closes (0: only after the close). A call costs ~230 ms whatever the length (the 30 s encoder window: 0.5 s of audio 233 ms, 5 s 299 ms, 8 s 326 ms on the M5, 2026-10-09), so decoding only the tail would not get under it; a pause the person talks through wastes one call. Its noise lines (subtitle credits, a bare 'Спасибо.') are dropped (pepin.voice_live.wake.is_hallucination)

brain.note: preset picks model + thinking + effort; keys beside it win (--set brain.effort=medium). --brain NAME at start; while running scripts/voice_cascade.py switch --brain NAME (built and warmed, it takes the next turn; the conversation goes on with it afresh, the old brain's history is not carried over). Thinking off: Haiku 5.5 'disabled'; Sonnet 5.5 'between_tools' (it refuses 'disabled'); Opus 5.5 cannot switch thinking off, 'adaptive' + effort low is its floor. Measured first word with a ~3k-token cached persona: Haiku 0.56 s, Sonnet 0.64 s, Opus 2.3 s; a tool round trip adds 1.4 s (Haiku) to 3.4 s (Sonnet). Gemini (provider gemini, GEMINI_API_KEY): thinking off is the lowest each model takes, probed 2026-10-09: 3.5 Flash-Lite refuses thinking_budget 0, takes thinking_level minimal; 3.5 Flash takes budget 0; 3.8 Flash takes budget 0 but still thinks (56 tokens on a greeting) and refuses minimal, so level low; its implicit cache needs a 4096-token prefix and has no write premium; keep_warm_s 0 (a warm-up would re-bill the whole prefix). Groq (provider openai: the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, GROQ_API_KEY; no retries, a 429 is printed): the free tier limits tokens per minute and a 3.5k-token prompt stalled 13-25 s in retries, so its presets take the compact persona and 7 tools with their descriptions cut to a sentence (compact_tools; ~1.3k tokens a call; this key's limit is 8000 input tokens a minute for both models, 2026-10-09); gpt-oss-120b with reasoning low, qwen3.8-27b as it comes. tool_choice required forces a call in a turn's first round (to try on a model that answers '...' instead of calling see). cache: a breakpoint on the persona (tools + persona, shared by every conversation) and on the growing conversation; prewarm: a max_tokens 0 call at start writes it, and again after keep_warm_s without a call (the cache lives 5 min). The key: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment

qwen3-vd.voice_description: Мягкий, тёплый голос молодой женщины; носительница русского языка, говорит спокойно, естественно и дружелюбно, с лёгкой улыбкой.

voice.note: preset picks engine, model, speaker and style handling from presets (keys beside it win); an engine's name (qwen3, gemini, say) stands for its first preset; --voice NAME at start, scripts/voice_cascade.py switch --voice NAME while running (the new voice loads beside the one speaking and takes the next sentence). The brain's {style} reaches a voice with use_style. qwen3-0.6b: Qwen3-TTS 0.6B CustomVoice serena through mlx-audio 0.5.8, no style (upstream drops the instruction on the 0.6B). qwen3-1.7b: 1.7B CustomVoice 8-bit serena, the style as Qwen's instruct. qwen3-vd: 1.7B VoiceDesign 8-bit, the voice in voice_description, the style appended to it, the sampler seeded (seed) so the timbre holds between sentences. On disk: 0.6B 1.8 GB, each 1.7B 2.9 GB (the 0.68 GB speech tokenizer shared), all three already in hf_home. 2026-10-09, warm, 3 Russian sentences x 4 styles x 2, the presets interleaved (scratch/tts_voices/presets_probe.py; the GPU shared with another Whisper benchmark): first audio median / p90 0.6b 112/263 ms, 1.7b 153/433, vd 118/449 (alone and quieter: 65, 80 ms); real-time factor 0.32, 0.39, 0.39; MLX memory 2.0, +3.1, +3.1 GB; load and warm-up 1.5-2 s a 1.7B. Russian style words (шёпотом, грустно, радостно) moved neither loudness nor length beyond the 0.6B's sampling spread; English ones did (Whispering very quietly: 1.7b -5 dB, vd -6 dB and 1.5x longer), so the personas ask for English style words. gemini-lite / gemini-flash: Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite / Flash TTS (GEMINI_API_KEY), streamed per sentence, the style in speech_metadata.style (2026-10-09: not read aloud, a whisper 11-13 dB quieter; written into the text the instruction IS read aloud); first audio lite 0.40-0.52 s, flash 0.63-0.69 s; ~0.06-0.09 (lite) and 0.12-0.14 (flash) US cents a 4-6 s sentence, in the ledger with the brain's. Its 30 prebuilt voices, all listed for Russian on both 3.8 TTS models (Kore checked: Whisper reads its Russian back word for word): Zephyr, Puck, Charon, Kore, Fenrir, Leda, Orus, Aoede, Callirrhoe, Autonoe, Enceladus, Iapetus, Umbriel, Algieba, Despina, Erinome, Algenib, Rasalgethi, Laomedeia, Achernar, Alnilam, Schedar, Gacrux, Pulcherrima, Achird, Zubenelgenubi, Vindemiatrix, Sadachbia, Sadaltager, Sulafat. fallback: the local preset that says a sentence when the call fails or brings no audio within cloud_timeout_s (the cloud then rests 30 s); cloud_max_calls: a run's cap on cloud calls (null: none). A cloud voice makes no clips at load; lines of 40 characters or fewer are kept in ~/.cache/pepin/tts by model, voice, style and text, so a line said once is free after. chunk_s 0.2 (2026-10-09, 1 to 15 words, 5 runs each): first chunk 61-115 ms against 185-203 ms at 0.5, with 0.07 s or more of audio always queued ahead of the speaker. hf_home: an HF cache already holding the weights (relative to the main checkout); missing there, the default cache is used. openers: the commonest first sentences, synthesised at load and played from memory when the brain says one without a style. say: macOS say, whole sentences at 16 kHz, for a test without the model gain_db (per preset): dB applied to the engine's own audio (a cloud voice's fallback keeps its level); Gemini voices come ~10 dB hotter than Qwen (-16 vs -26 dBFS speech, 2026-10-11), so -10 keeps the room and the echo guard at one level.

player.note: the pacer runs lead_s ahead of the speaker in block_s blocks: the jitter buffer over WiFi (0.5 s, as the Live loop), and what a barge-in has to silence (the board flushes it). It does not delay the first sample: the first block goes at once

flags.note: barge_in: while Pepin speaks, a voice over the barge_in threshold for hold_s flushes the speaker at once and cuts the conversation to what was heard; the person's words become the next turn (off: the mic is shut while Pepin speaks, as in the Live loop). backchannel: a short local clip when the person pauses mid-utterance. prosody_tags: Praat's numbers against the running baseline as a tag line in front of the person's words

barge_in.note: detector (pepin.voice_cascade.barge_in) decides that the person cuts in while a reply plays. level: a frame over_floor_db above the room's floor and at least min_dbfs is voice, hold_s of voice cuts in (a quiet frame takes back half a frame). vad: Silero VAD (vad_model silero-v6: v6.2.3 from its repository, MIT, 2.3 MB, fetched once into ~/.cache/pepin and SHA-256 checked; silero-v5: the Hub's v5; or a file), 0.08 ms a 32 ms chunk; a frame is voice at p >= vad_threshold, at least vad_min_dbfs and echo_margin_db over the robot's predicted echo (the level the player sent echo_lag_s earlier, less echo_loss_db), vad_hold_s of it cuts in. words: words_gate held words_listen_s sends the voice (at most words_window_s, a call at most every words_every_s) to Whisper; a word that is not a backchannel, laughter, a noise line or the robot's own sentence cuts in. 2026-10-09, 16 live conversations, 184 replies, 52 with the person's words over them (scripts/barge_in_eval.py: each loud moment of a reply read by Whisper), caught / false / median reaction after the voice's onset: the live runs (level) 41/9/239 ms; level 43/6/289; vad v5 hold 0.2 41/0/540, hold 0.1 44/1/407; vad v6 hold 0.2 42/1/359, 0.15 43/1/315, 0.1 45/2/245 (the two false: laughter at a reply's start, and a sound Whisper reads as its noise lines); words 36/2/740 (both false ones late catches of real speech: the canceller mangles a voice over the robot's and Whisper needs ~0.5 s more). The false barge-ins of the level gate are the room (knocks, rustle: 10.5 bursts a minute while the robot speaks, 13.7 while silent), not the echo: the mic sits at the room's floor while the robot plays at -18.5 dBFS, so the echo guard (>= 45 dB of loss measured) does not bind today; it is there for a canceller that loses convergence. Every barge-in is logged (events.jsonl barge_in: reason, level, the array's direction)

backchannel.note: a clip (synthesised once at load) when the person has been quiet delay_s inside an utterance of at least min_speech_s, before the end of the turn

prosody.speaker: Артём
prosody.stretch_note: a drawn-out vowel joins the tag line spelled as people write one, [Артём: растянуто: прииинтер]: a vowel at least stretch_ratio times this person's usual vowel in its place (the running median; a phrase's last vowel apart) and stretch_min_s long; null ratio: never. Needs transcriber.gigaam.timings. 2026-10-12 (scratch/gigaam_timing_1012/stretch_eval.py, the e2e-rnnt's tokens): Artem's usual vowel 0.10 s, a phrase's last 0.13 s (162 far-field utterances); 'а при́нтер' of cascade_144219 (his stress correction) called прииинтер, 0.36 s x2.8; on the 162 ordinary utterances 7.4 % of words are called (x2.5 and 0.3 s: 3.5 %), most of them his own drawls while thinking (температуруууу, ууумеешь, нуууу); a vowel lengthened x3 by PSOLA called 21 of 40 times, the right letter 14 (a vowel shorter than 0.08 s stays under the floor)
prosody.note: the tag line names speaker while person recognition is off (config/people.json, switch people; on, it names the recognised person, [говорит: Саша; тише обычного], each person with a baseline of their own, and nobody unknown gets prosody words), says nothing until min_baseline utterances are in the running baseline (the last window of this run), and gives a word for each number at least z of the person's spreads from their mean (2.0: Artem's deliberate contrasts sit at 2.7-6 sd, and with five numbers z 1.0 flagged 8 of the 10 tagged phrases of the 2026-10-08 bench): loudness, rate (syllables/s), pitch (median, st), intonation (5-95 % range, st), long pauses. emotion_model: null, audeering (arousal joins the numbers; CC-BY-NC-SA research weights, 0.7 GB) or emotion2vec (its label quoted; needs funasr installed). scratch/prosody_1008/REPORT.md: the plain numbers separate Artem's deliberate contrasts by 2.7-6 sd; the label models contradict each other

conversation.note: tool_filler: said locally (a clip made at load) when the brain calls a slow tool (see, look, find...) before saying a word in its reply; empty: off. a conversation closes after idle_close_s without the person's voice or a reply (never while a drive runs), on a goodbye, on end_conversation, or at max_session_s. report_drive_start: a drive answers its call when the goal server takes it (the brain says its acknowledgement) and its end comes as a [robot] turn. error_line: said locally when the brain fails before saying anything

prices_usd_per_mtok.note: Anthropic list prices (the claude-api reference, cached 2026-10-06): cache reads 0.1x input (0.05x on Opus 5.5), 5-minute cache writes 1.25x. Haiku 5.5 prompts over 100k tokens cost more (never reached here). Gemini (the coordinator's figures, 2026-10-09): cached input at the cached rate, no write premium. Gemini TTS (the coordinator's figures, 2026-10-09): text in, audio out at 25 tokens a second of speech, no cache

money.note: a conversation that would break a cap is never opened; the estimates (brain and cloud voice) are kept in data/voice/cascade_ledger.jsonl
